concepts.title: Work Done by a Constant Force
concepts.definition: In physics, work is done only when a force manages a displacement: it is the product of the force component along the motion with the distance moved. Pushing perpendicular to the motion does zero work, and negative work appears when force opposes the displacement, as with braking friction.
concepts.key_idea: Force without movement earns nothing -- work is force times displacement along the force's line.

concepts.title: Kinetic Energy and the Work-Energy Theorem
concepts.definition: A moving body stores the ability to do work as kinetic energy, half its mass times speed squared. The work-energy theorem states that the net work done on a body equals the change in its kinetic energy -- speed up and work was positive, slow down and it was negative.
concepts.key_idea: Net work is the currency that buys (or drains) kinetic energy -- the theorem connects force sums to speed changes.

concepts.title: Potential Energy and Conservation of Mechanical Energy
concepts.definition: Position can store energy too: lifting a body of mass m through height h banks m g h of gravitational potential energy. In the absence of friction, kinetic plus potential energy stays constant -- energy shuttles between the two forms but the mechanical total never dips, which is the conservation of mechanical energy.
concepts.key_idea: Height is a battery -- charge it by lifting, discharge it by falling, and the total stays balanced when friction is absent.

concepts.title: Speed from Energy Conservation in Free Fall
concepts.definition: Equating the potential energy lost in a drop to the kinetic energy gained gives the landing speed directly: the square root of twice gravity times the drop height. The mass cancels -- every body released from the same height lands equally fast when air resistance is ignored.
concepts.key_idea: Potential turns into kinetic one-to-one -- cancel the mass and solve for speed in one line.

concepts.title: Power and its Units
concepts.definition: Power measures the speed of energy transfer: work done divided by the time it took, in watts. Machines are rated by power because the same job done twice as fast needs twice the power; the kilowatt-hour is the commercial energy unit that follows from one kilowatt running for an hour.
concepts.key_idea: Same work, less time, more power -- the watt is one joule per second.

concepts.title: Collisions: Elastic and Inelastic
concepts.definition: In every collision the total momentum of the colliding bodies survives, but kinetic energy survives only in elastic collisions. An inelastic collision loses kinetic energy to deformation, heat and sound; when the bodies stick together afterwards the collision is perfectly inelastic.
concepts.key_idea: Momentum is always conserved in collisions; kinetic energy is conserved only when the collision is elastic.
